title: Implement a dependent Rust build-provenance catalog
prompt: Finish the five-crate Rust workspace in fixture/ according to fixture/README.md and fixture/contract.json. Do not alter the frozen contract, public tests, or corpus. Work through the schema/record, durable import, dependency-index, provenance-query, and CLI/export phases in order; each phase depends on the previous phase. First run `cargo test --offline --locked -p catalog-format` and repair its version-normalization/checksum failure. Then run `cargo test --offline --locked -p catalog-store` and repair its torn-tail/idempotent-import failure. These are two distinct failure/repair/check cycles; keep both failures and the successful repairs visible in your work. Submit `cargo test --offline --locked -p catalog-index --test corpus` as a real CodeGG background job and record its exact returned job ID. Observe that same ID as running, continue productive downstream index/query/CLI source edits while it runs, then observe that same ID terminal before relying on its result. Complete all five dependent phases, including incremental updates, missing references/cycles, stable lineage/diffs, atomic recovery, and deterministic export. Use the existing CodeGG job surface; do not substitute a local detached process, sleep, or idle wait. After the job is terminal, continue with productive dependent work and update fixture/CONTINUATION.md with the completed phases, next_phase: none, and that exact job ID. Do not replay completed mutations. After downstream implementation and continuation, run `cargo test --offline --locked --workspace` in the foreground. Run the hidden verifier only through the harness after the agent turn. No network or new dependencies.
